evidence_detail: 257 = 226 NBS514 (all carry a source_id, e.g. nbs514:p37:010) + 31 ThermoML (23 docs). The count is robust: 147/257 also clear the phase test on a real mp, so >=100 survives losing all 110 assumed-mp rows. But 'all 257 phase-verified liquid' is not supported - 110/257 use mp=ASSUMED_C (85x1.0, 18x2.0, 6x3.0, 1x-1.0) and 9 have mp_margin<5 K. Duplicate risk: 2 same-substance pairs -> <=255 distinct substances: limonene XMGQYMWWDOXHJM-UHFFFAOYSA-N (2.30) vs XMGQYMWWDOXHJM-JTQLQIEISA-N (2.36), identical constitutional SMILES CC1=CCC(CC1)C(=C)C; propenylbenzene QROGIFZRVHSFLM-UHFFFAOYSA-N (2.63, named '3-Phenyl-1-propene' but PubChem CID 12500 = prop-1-enylbenzene, allylbenzene C6H5CH2CH=CH2 is a different skeleton) vs QROGIFZRVHSFLM-QHHAFSJGSA-N (2.73). Allylbenzene (NBS ref 215, p39:010) is therefore absent from the 257 and a duplicate propenylbenzene is present. identity_audit_b100.json (MATCH 257) and smiles_verification (SAME 240 / STEREO_ONLY 17, 0 dup CID) cannot see this because both rows are internally consistent SMILES->InChIKey.

392/392 audit rows are STATIC_BY_SOURCE_DEFINITION; expansion_frequency_mhz blank 392/392 and transcription_frequency_note blank 392/392 (nbs514_condition_audit.csv). The 127-row exclusion is real: 127 transcription rows carry f=3.6-5e8 cycles/sec (57x5e8, 35x4e8, 27x3.6e8, 9 spaced variants), and 0/127 are in dielectric_pool_expansion_observations.csv, 0/226 admitted molecules has a note. 244 unselected rows = 127 frequency + 117 other (140 two_or_less, 16 candidate_exception). Caveats that force INFERRED rather than DOCUMENTED: (a) the status is assigned mechanically by an empty note (build_b100_asset_inventory.py L167-170 - 'STATIC_BY_SOURCE_DEFINITION' if src and not has_note), it is a labelling convention, not per-row evidence; (b) excluding high-frequency rows does not by itself prove the rest are static - it proves only that they carry no high-frequency footnote (it does not, and cannot, be a non-sequitur test because the audit is built from the already-filtered set); (c) 37/226 admitted molecules cite a primary reference that also produced a high-frequency row (e.g. nbs514:p35:007 m-Xylene refs 3,12,16,35,107,116,207,229; nbs514:p41:004 1-bromonaphthalene refs 272 [7,12]); (d) 226 molecules rest on 122 distinct NBS ref numbers (272 -> 23 molecules, 82 -> 19, 7 -> 18); (e) frequency_note is absent from raw_line (0/636) so the 127 exclusions can only be re-verified against the printed PDF, not from the transcription.

110/257 phase decisions rest on a fabricated mp. pubchem_mp_lookup_b100.csv notes start ASSUMED_C: fetch_pubchem_mp_b100.py L144-163 accepts the first bare number in -150..400 from any property string; 85 rows are literally the '1' of 'InChI=1S/...' (e.g. C9H19BrO, 1-bromo-2-ethoxyheptane -> 1.0 C), 18 are 2.0, 6 are 3.0, 1 is -1.0. audit_b100_phase_state.py ignores the note, stamps mp_source=PUBCHEM_PUGVIEW, has_mp_data=true, and passes any mp<T_C. Only 147/257 have a parsed value (67 CONVERTED_FROM_F, 43 OK, 35 HSDB, 1 PAC, 1 ILO). The same extractor reads normal boiling points as melting points and rejects real liquids: 1-Iodopentane 'OK: 157 C @760 [mm Hg]', Diiodomethane 181, Isoamyl ether 172.5, Isobutyl benzoate 242, Butyl nitrate 136, 1,3-bis(CF3)benzene 116, 3-Heptanol '66 C (20 mm Hg)' - 7 of the 14 SOLID_OR_SUPERCOOLED exclusions are boiling points, not melting points. Unchecked solid risk inside the 257: FKHNZQFCDGOQGV-UHFFFAOYSA-N 2,3-dimethylquinoxaline admitted with mp=2.0 C at T=298.15 K although its PubChem record carries no melting point at all. Marginal admits: N-methylacetamide 2.0 K, diethanolamine 2.1 K, butyl stearate 3.0 K, phenyl ether 3.2 K margin.

One compendium supplies 226/257 (88%) and inside it sit 122 distinct primary refs, so it is neither 226 independent measurements nor a single laboratory. The 31 Q1 labels rest on 23 distinct ThermoML documents; 18 of the 31 have only one document. Molecules with >=2 programmes: 19 (14x2, 4x3, 1x5). The '18 corroborated' number is substantively correct but the flag is presence-only (audit_b100_source_independence.py L132/149: in_both = expansion obs AND ledger doc, no value test): 12 of the 18 appear in cross_source_agree_b100.csv, 6 do not - VFWCMGCRMGJXDK 1-Chlorobutane, NHTMVDHEPJAVLT 2,2,4-Trimethylpentane, KWOLFJPFCHCOCG Acetophenone, VZGDMQKNWNREIO Carbon tetrachloride, LQNUZADURLCDLV Nitrobenzene, SNRUBQQJIBEYMU n-Dodecane. I compared those 6 with measurement_ledger_v1.csv at the same T and all agree (CCl4 2.238 vs 2.230, nitrobenzene 34.82 vs 34.78, 2,2,4-TMP 1.94 vs 1.94, acetophenone 17.39 vs 17.51, dodecane 2.014 vs 2.030, 1-chlorobutane 7.39 vs ~7.28 interpolated), so 18 holds - but the JSON sentence 'NBS and ThermoML both have eps and they agree' is unsupported for those 6 by any recorded test. '30 independent programmes' = 1 compendium + 29 documents, of which only 23 carry Q1 labels; source_registry_b100.csv lists 62 sources and 32 of them contribute nothing to the 257. Separately, all 11 cross-source conflicts were deleted by the admission gate, so no admitted molecule can be a conflict - the agreement is built in, not observed.

31/31 Q1 labels reproduce an exact measurement_ledger_v1.csv record (same T_K and epsilon): 243 records, 100% traceability_status=TRACEABLE, 100% phase=Liquid, 0 null source_document_id, pressure 91.3-101.325 kPa, source_file_sha256 and source_row_index present, 23 distinct DOIs (e.g. butan-2-ol BTANRVKWQNVYAZ-N 16.6 @298.15 from 10.1016/j.fluid.2013.12.014;10.1021/je3007666;10.1021/je800593p;10.1021/je900503p). All 226 Q2 carry only compendium-level conditions, so the split is applied as claimed and no Q1 label is a v04 aggregate artefact (0 Q1 molecules in reconstruction_exceptions.csv). Caveats: frequency_mhz=0.0 on all 243 Q1 records (only 20/263 core records are nonzero - 0.05-3 MHz - and none belongs to a Q1 molecule), so 'per-measurement provenance' covers T, P, eps and document but NOT frequency; 6 dual-layer molecules are graded Q2 despite full ThermoML records (conservative, but it means Q2 does not imply 'no per-measurement provenance'); Q1 does not imply independently corroborated (18/31 are single-document) and within-1K spread reaches 6.1% (butan-2-ol 16.58-17.60).

147 overlap = 136 AGREE + 11 CONFLICT, but only 12 of the 136 and 0 of the 11 are in the 257: the admission gate drops every conflict (build_b100_admission_gate.py L230, L245-246, L275-276, 'CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED'), so the dataset's clean cross-source record is an artefact of the gate. 122/136 AGREE rows also rest on v04 core values whose condition pair is flagged invalid in reconstruction_exceptions.csv. The '11 genuinely unresolved' claim is overstated: 5 comparison values are documented invalid (SYNTHETIC_PAIR_FROM_INDEPENDENT_MEDIAN: cyclohexanone JHIVVAPYMSGYDF, pentan-1-ol AMQJEAYHLZJPGS, hexan-1-ol ZSIAUFGUXNUGDI, butan-1-ol LRHPLDYGYMQRHN; NO_CONTRIBUTING_MEASUREMENT: 1,4-dichlorobutane KJDRSWPQXHESDQ) and methylcyclohexane UAEPNZWRGJTJPN 2.010 vs 2.02 is a 1.4% agreement mislabelled only because delta_T=5.05 K exceeded the 5.0 K tolerance. Re-comparing NBS against the ledger at the NBS temperature: within 5% -> methylcyclohexane 1.4%, 2-methylpropan-2-ol 3.9%, formamide 4.4%, 1,2-ethanediol 4.6%; beyond 5% -> cyclohexanone 13.8%, pentan-1-ol 13.8%, propan-1-ol 9.7%, 1,2-propanediol 9.2%, hexan-1-ol 6.7%, butan-1-ol 6.5%; 1,4-dichlorobutane has no ledger measurement at all. Net: ~6 conflicts survive a like-for-like check, ~5 do not, and the remaining ones were never adjudicated - they were removed.
